subjects.description: small red rectangular mass hanging from lower end of vertical spring

observation.what_happens: A red block hangs from a vertical spring and oscillates up and down. The motion is already underway at the start and continues oscillating through the end of the clip.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The track is 1D vertical with x constant and s swinging ~120 px with ~0.8 s period and only weak amplitude change, classic mass-spring SHM. Candidates go from ideal to linearly damped to quadratic air drag to cubic Duffing stiffness to test what, if anything, beats a perfect sine on unseen data.

critique.finding: The block swings on a spring with tone {omega0} around spot {s_eq} while air drag {gamma} slowly steals energy. It only partly captures the motion with a clear wave left in the misses.
critique.headline: Spring block keeps bouncing as air gently slows it
critique.revision_idea: Test a Duffing spring that adds a cubic stiffness term to the linear pull. The misses alternate with the swing instead of scattering randomly, which is the classic sign of frequency that shifts with amplitude.
critique.why_it_won: It matches the steady back-and-forth bounce that straight-fall and steady-push laws cannot make at all.

headline: A law drawn by public randomness, its round named before it existed: a linear spring with viscous damping and a drive. The drive was found by code's fallback; the winning law also carries a small cubic term the drawn law does not have.
finding: A spring whose stiffness changes when stretched a lot, plus a little friction. Plus a periodic drive F·cos(ω_d t + φ), added by code at the unexplained residual frequency 5.97 rad/s. Measured: small-amplitude natural frequency 7.8385 ± 0.0029 rad/s; static equilibrium position 82.997 ± 0.057 px; linear viscous damping rate 0.20358 ± 0.00068 1/s.

eyeball.confidence: low - single still frame provided, no time-series to fit; values are typical-order guesses for a small lab mass-spring
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical damped harmonic oscillator about static equilibrium: x double-dot + gamma x-dot + omega0^2*(x - s_eq) = 0, filmed from the side so vertical displacement appears along the image vertical/track coordinate

clockCheck.why: Clock not checked: with no ruler in view and no length stated, gravity can’t be measured in metres. A slowed clip would look the same.

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6606498). The round was named in 078bdc5 and pushed before it existed; the law's SHA-256 was pushed in 3d5237d before the clip was rendered; the run used commit 6514586 on a clean tree; the law was revealed in cd70ce2. Missed under the rule, with the drive found by code. The drawn law was a linear spring with viscous damping and a periodic drive at 6.194 rad/s. The misses of Muse Spark's best law peaked at 5.97 rad/s, 113 times the noise, labelled unexplained, and code built that law (a Duffing spring with viscous damping) plus a drive started there, held back from the referee's table. The referee asked for a cubic stiffness; Muse Wonder was never called, because fitting the first pool and code's fallback took 575 s of the run's 600 s budget. Code's drive then entered and won: drive frequency 6.1956 ± 0.0014 rad/s against 6.194 (1.1σ), drive strength 0.6054 ± 0.0010 m/s² against 0.6077 (2.3σ), damping 0.2036 ± 0.0007 against 0.2029 (1.0σ), natural frequency 7.8385 ± 0.0029 against 7.8294 (3.1σ). Its cubic term, −6.8 ± 2.1 × 10⁻⁵ per px² s² (3.2σ, a slight softening), is present where the drawn spring is linear, so the term set differs. It predicts the unseen frames to 1.2 times the noise. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.

si.scale: the render's own scale, 0.00128 m per pixel (orthographic camera)

drawn.equation: x'' = -(k/m) x - b x' + F0 cos(wd t)
drawn.x: displacement below the resting point (m, down positive); t from release

F0.rule: F0 / |w0^2 - wd^2| = share of A uniform in [0.15, 0.35] (drawn 0.248)

wd.rule: wd / w0 uniform in [0.55, 0.8] or [1.25, 1.6], each half the time (drawn 0.791)

sealed.narration: a block on a spring, filmed from the side
sealed.rule: found only if the winner's term set equals the drawn term set, a fitted term whose constant is within 2σ of zero counting as absent, and every shared constant is within 2σ of the drawn value
sealed.terms: winner (code: Muse Spark's Duffing law plus the fallback drive at the unexplained residual peak): linear (ω₀), cubic β = −0.000068 ± 0.000021 (3.2σ, present), viscous γ = 0.20358 ± 0.00068 (300σ, present), drive F = 472.9 ± 0.8 px/s² (602σ, present) at ω_d = 6.1956 ± 0.0014; drawn: linear, viscous, drive. Term sets differ: an extra cubic term.

spectrumAtScoring.summary: Residual spectrum of “Nonlinear spring with damping” on the fitted frames (its misses, fitted as sinusoids one at a time, strongest first): strongest at ω = 5.97 rad/s (period 1.053 s), amplitude 113 × the noise (16.8 px in s): UNEXPLAINED, a peak at ω = 5.97 rad/s that is not the motion's frequency, a harmonic, a drift or noise; a periodic drive F·cos(ωt+φ) with ω near this value is the usual cause; a drive whose fitted frequency slides onto the motion's own frequency is not a drive; next at ω = 8.38 rad/s (period 0.750 s), amplitude 23.9 × the noise (3.54 px in s): the motion's own frequency (the law's own frequency, damping or amplitude is off), not a drive; next at ω = 9.68 rad/s (period 0.649 s), amplitude 21.4 × the noise (3.17 px in s): UNEXPLAINED, a peak at ω = 9.68 rad/s that is not the motion's frequency, a harmonic, a drift or noise; a periodic drive F·cos(ωt+φ) with ω near this value is the usual cause; a drive whose fitted frequency slides onto the motion's own frequency is not a drive. The motion's own frequency is 7.91 rad/s.
spectrumAtScoring.note: The labels are the run's own (code 6514586 labelled the spectrum, passed Muse Wonder the labelled summary and a residual_spectrum tool, and held code's drive back as a fallback).
